transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I can’t think straight at work—decisions that used to be easy now leave me stuck and second‑guessing everything. This decline in my concentration actually came up during a recent performance check-in, which led my HR partner to suggest an occupational medicine consult and eventually this evaluation.
Did these difficulties with concentration and decision-making start following a specific stressful life event, or have you noticed these patterns recurring over several years?

I’ve actually noticed milder patterns of these highs and crashes cycling since my mid-twenties, but they became much worse and impossible to ignore over the past year. The severe issues with my concentration really escalated after the stress of my promotion to lead a high-pressure lean transformation project, and this current low spell has been dragging on for about three months now.

During those 'high' periods you mentioned experiencing since your mid-twenties, did you ever have times where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing and you were taking on too many projects at once?

Yes, absolutely. During those times I'd sleep only three or four hours a night but feel completely fine, and I'd pack my schedule with extra projects and plant visits. My coworkers even joked that I was on "1.5x speed" because I talked so fast and jumped constantly from one idea to the next.
During your current three-month low, have you experienced any thoughts of wanting to end your life, or have you felt completely unable to function in your daily activities?

I haven't had any thoughts of wanting to end my life, but my ability to function at work has been severely impacted. I've been missing key deadlines and had to hand off parts of my flagship project to colleagues. My manager has even warned me that they may have to reconsider my role on the transformation team if I can't get back to my usual level.

During this current three-month period, have you felt completely unable to function in your daily activities, such as being unable to eat, bathe, or take care of your basic needs, or is your impairment primarily limited to your work performance?

While I'm still managing basic hygiene, the impairment is definitely most severe at work where I'm missing deadlines and facing a potential change in my role. However, my daily life is absolutely affected too; I've completely lost my appetite and barely eat, and even basic movements feel like I'm trying to walk underwater. Everything just takes immense physical effort right now.

Beyond the fatigue and appetite loss, have you experienced any periods during these past three months where you felt completely unable to experience any pleasure or interest in your usual hobbies, or felt a distinct, heavy sense of worthlessness or guilt?
I haven't really experienced those specific feelings of guilt or a loss of interest in my hobbies. Mostly, I just feel this heavy, hollow emptiness and a complete lack of energy.
During these past three months, have you felt so slowed down physically and mentally that others have noticed you moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?

Yes, during this three-month low, I have felt incredibly slowed down both physically and mentally. My team has actually commented that I move like I'm "underwater"—I walk slowly, stare at my screen, and even typing an email or reaching for my notebook takes a massive, deliberate effort.

During these past three months, have you felt so severely slowed down or incapacitated that you have been unable to perform your basic daily tasks, such as getting out of bed for most of the day or maintaining your personal hygiene?

No, I haven't been completely bedridden or unable to maintain my hygiene over these past three months, but I am extremely slowed down. It constantly feels like I'm moving underwater, where just typing an email or reaching for my notebook takes a deliberate physical effort. This sluggishness has severely impacted my ability to keep up with my work tasks and make basic decisions.
During these past three months, have you experienced any days where you felt so incapacitated that you were unable to get out of bed or perform almost any of your basic daily responsibilities?

Over these past three months, I haven't been completely bedridden because I force myself to get out of bed and go to work. However, once I'm there, every single action feels like I'm moving underwater and takes immense physical effort. Because of this, my work functioning has severely suffered, leading to missed deadlines and having to hand off my tasks to colleagues.
